items.title: Temple Styles — Nagara, Dravida & Vesara
items.body:
## Core temple parts

- **Garbhagriha** — the 'womb-house' sanctum holding the deity.
- **Shikhara** (North) / **Vimana** (South) — the tower over the sanctum.
- **Mandapa** — pillared hall before the sanctum; **Gopuram** — the gateway tower of a South Indian complex; **Pradakshina path** — circumambulatory passage.

## The three styles

| Feature | Nagara (North) | Dravida (South) | Vesara (Deccan) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tower | curvilinear, pointed **shikhara** | pyramidal, tiered **vimana** | hybrid of the two |
| Enclosure | usually no tall gateways | compound wall with **gopurams** | intermediate |
| Examples | Kandariya Mahadeva (Khajuraho), Konark | Brihadeeswarar (Thanjavur), Meenakshi (Madurai) | Hoysaleswara (Halebidu) |

## Nagara sub-schools

- **Kalinga** (Odisha): beehive **deula** tower + front **jagamohana** hall — Lingaraj (Somavamsi, 11th c.), Jagannath Puri (Ganga, 12th c.), **Konark Sun Temple** (Narasimhadeva I, 13th c.).

## Dravida sub-styles

- **Pallava** (7th–9th c.) — rock-cut & monolithic, Mahabalipuram Shore Temple.
- **Chola** (9th–13th c.) — colossal vimanas, Brihadeeswarar, Thanjavur.
- **Pandya** (13th–16th c.) — first great **gopurams** (Srirangam).
- **Vijayanagara** (14th–17th c.) — huge gopurams & complexes, Virupaksha, Hampi.
- **Vesara/Hoysala** — Belur, Halebidu; **Chalukya** — Badami/Pattadakal.
keyPoints: Garbhagriha = sanctum; shikhara (North)/vimana (South) = sanctum tower; gopuram = South Indian gateway tower.
Nagara = curvilinear shikhara (North); Dravida = pyramidal vimana + gopuram enclosures (South); Vesara = hybrid of both (Deccan).
Kalinga (Odisha) sub-style: deula tower + jagamohana hall — Lingaraj, Jagannath Puri, Konark.
Dravida phases: Pallava (rock-cut) → Chola (giant vimana) → Pandya (gopurams) → Vijayanagara (colossal gopurams, Hampi).
Vesara/Hoysala temples (Belur, Halebidu) blend Nagara and Dravida forms in the Deccan.
items.mnemonic: 'North Curves, South Pyramids, Deccan Mixes' — Nagara shikhara curves, Dravida vimana is pyramidal, Vesara mixes.
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Temple Architecture; Kalinga & Dravida styles

figure.caption: Nagara (curvilinear shikhara), Dravida (vimana + gopuram), Vesara (Deccan hybrid).

items.title: Cave (Rock-cut) Architecture
items.body:
## Origins & sects

- Rock-cut caves began in the **Mauryan period** — the **Barabar Caves** (near Gaya) donated to the **Ajivika sect**; the **Lomas Rishi** cave is the earliest, imitating timber form.
- Later caves served **Buddhist** (2nd c. BCE–5th c. CE), **Jain** (5th–10th c.) and **Hindu** (from 5th c.) worship.

## Chaitya vs Vihara

| | Chaitya | Vihara |
|---|---|---|
| Use | prayer hall with a **stupa** | monastery / monks' residence |
| Plan | apsidal, arched (horseshoe) roof | cells around a central court |
| Example | Great Chaitya, **Karla** (Cave 8) | Ajanta, Kanheri viharas |

## Landmark cave sites

- **Ajanta** (Maharashtra) — 30 Buddhist caves; masterpieces of **fresco painting**; discovered 1819 (John Smith); UNESCO 1983.
- **Ellora** — 34 caves of **all three faiths** (17 Hindu, 12 Buddhist, 5 Jain); the **Kailasa Temple** (largest monolithic excavation) by Rashtrakuta **Krishna I**; UNESCO.
- **Elephanta** (8th c., basalt) — Shaivite; famed **Trimurti** of Shiva; UNESCO 1987.
- **Badami** (Chalukya, 6th c.) — earliest Brahmanical cave paintings.
keyPoints: Earliest rock-cut caves = Mauryan Barabar Caves (Ajivika sect); Lomas Rishi is the oldest, copying timber architecture.
Chaitya = prayer hall with a stupa (Karla, Cave 8 = largest); Vihara = monastery with monks' cells.
Ajanta = 30 Buddhist caves, finest ancient frescoes, discovered 1819, UNESCO 1983.
Ellora has all three faiths (34 caves); Kailasa Temple = largest monolith, by Rashtrakuta Krishna I.
Elephanta (8th c.) is Shaivite, famed for the Trimurti of Shiva (UNESCO 1987).
items.mnemonic: 'A-E-E' painting-faiths-Trimurti: Ajanta (paintings), Ellora (all faiths + Kailasa), Elephanta (Trimurti).
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Cave Architecture

items.title: Sculpture Schools, Pottery, Stupa & Ashokan Edicts
items.body:
## Sculpture schools (c. 1st–3rd c. CE)

| School | Material / Trait | Patron / Region |
|---|---|---|
| **Gandhara** | grey schist, **Greco-Roman** Buddha | Kushana north-west |
| **Mathura** | indigenous **red sandstone** | Kushana, Yamuna |
| **Amaravati** | white **marble** narrative reliefs | **Satavahana**, Krishna delta (AP) |

## Pottery sequence

- **OCP → PGW → NBPW** (Ochre Coloured Ware → Painted Grey Ware → Northern Black Polished Ware). PGW = later-Vedic doab; NBPW = luxury ware of the second urbanisation.

## Stupa

- A stupa (e.g. **Sanchi**, **Amaravati**) has the hemispherical **anda**, **harmika**, **chhatra** (umbrella), and a railing (**vedika**) pierced by **toranas** (gateways).

## Ashokan pillars & edicts

- Monolithic **Chunar sandstone** shafts with a mirror **polish**; the **Lion Capital, Sarnath** = India's national emblem; Ashoka Chakra = **24 spokes**.
- Scripts/languages: **Brahmi/Prakrit** in the core; **Kharoshthi/Aramaic** in the north-west; **Aramaic + Greek** in Afghanistan.
keyPoints: Gandhara = Greco-Roman grey-schist Buddha; Mathura = indigenous red sandstone; Amaravati = white-marble reliefs under the Satavahanas (AP).
Pottery order: OCP → PGW → NBPW; NBPW is the deluxe ware of the second urbanisation.
Stupa parts: anda, harmika, chhatra, vedika (railing) and torana (gateway).
Ashokan pillars = monolithic Chunar sandstone with high polish; Lion Capital of Sarnath is the national emblem (Chakra = 24 spokes).
Ashokan edicts: Brahmi/Prakrit in the core, Kharoshthi/Aramaic in the north-west, Aramaic + Greek in Afghanistan.
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Indian Sculpture and Pottery; Edicts and Inscriptions

items.title: Indo-Islamic Architecture
items.body:
## Concept

A fusion of Indian **trabeate** construction (pillars, brackets, lintels) with Islamic **arcuate** technique (**arches and domes** built with voussoirs, on squinches/pendentives). Bans on living forms produced **arabesque, geometric patterns and calligraphy**.

## Typical features

- **Charbagh** four-quartered gardens (paradise symbol), **jaali** lattice screens, **pietra dura** inlay, polychrome tile work, **minars** for the azaan.
- Building types: **mosque, tomb, dargah, minar, sarai, madrasa, charbagh**.

## Styles & examples

| Style | Example |
|---|---|
| **Imperial (Delhi Sultanate)** | Qutub Minar, Alai Darwaza, Quwwat-ul-Islam |
| **Provincial** | Atala Masjid (Jaunpur), Sidi Saiyyed jaalis (Gujarat), Bengal |
| **Mughal** | Humayun's Tomb, Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Fatehpur Sikri |
| **Deccani** | Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur), Charminar, Golconda |

- **Adhai Din Ka Jhopra** (Ajmer) reused temple pillars; **Gol Gumbaz** has a whispering gallery and a giant dome.
keyPoints: Indo-Islamic = Indian trabeate + Islamic arcuate (arches/domes via voussoirs, squinches/pendentives).
Signature features: charbagh gardens, jaali screens, pietra dura inlay, calligraphy/arabesque, minars.
Imperial (Sultanate): Qutub Minar, Alai Darwaza; Mughal: Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb, Red Fort.
Provincial styles: Jaunpur (Atala Masjid), Gujarat (Sidi Saiyyed jaalis), Bengal.
Deccani style: Gol Gumbaz (whispering gallery, Bijapur), Charminar & Golconda (Hyderabad).
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Indo-Islamic Architecture

items.title: Painting, Colonial & Modern Architecture
items.body:
## Painting

- **Ajanta** frescoes = finest ancient Buddhist murals; **Bagh** (MP) is a related, more earthly tradition.
- **Miniature schools**: **Mughal** (zenith under **Jahangir**), **Rajput/Rajasthani**, **Pahari** (Basohli, Kangra); **Tanjore** panel painting uses gold foil & gesso in the South.

## Colonial architecture

- **Portuguese** — Baroque/Iberian (Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa — UNESCO).
- **French** — Cartesian grid urban planning (Puducherry, Chandernagore; **Yanam** in AP).
- **British** — **Indo-Gothic/Victorian** (Victoria Memorial, Gateway of India, **CSMT** Mumbai — UNESCO); **Indo-Saracenic** fused Indian domes/chhatris/jaalis with Gothic; post-1911 **Neo-Classical** New Delhi by **Lutyens & Herbert Baker** (Rashtrapati Bhavan's 'upturned' dome).

## Modern architects

| Architect | Signature |
|---|---|
| **Le Corbusier** | plan of **Chandigarh**, first planned city |
| **Laurie Baker** | 'Architect of the Poor', filler-slab eco housing, Kerala |
| **Charles Correa** | Jawahar Kala Kendra (Jaipur), MP Assembly; Padma Vibhushan 2006 |
keyPoints: Ajanta = finest ancient frescoes; Mughal miniatures peaked under Jahangir; Rajput, Pahari (Kangra/Basohli) and Tanjore are other schools.
British colonial: Indo-Gothic (Victoria Memorial, Gateway of India, CSMT), Indo-Saracenic, and post-1911 Neo-Classical New Delhi (Lutyens & Baker).
French colonial architecture used Cartesian grid town planning (Puducherry, Yanam in AP).
Le Corbusier planned Chandigarh; Laurie Baker = 'Architect of the Poor' (filler slab); Charles Correa won the Padma Vibhushan (2006).
Vidhana Soudha (Bengaluru) is Neo-Dravidian; Lotus Temple is a modern Bahá'í house of worship.
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Indian Paintings; Modern Architecture

items.title: UNESCO Sites of India & Andhra Pradesh Art
items.body:
## UNESCO World Heritage Sites of India (as of 2026)

- India has **45 sites** — **37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed** (Khangchendzonga NP). India ranks **6th** worldwide.
- **First four (1983)**: **Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, Taj Mahal**.
- Recent inscriptions:

| Site | Year |
|---|---|
| Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas; Santiniketan | 2023 |
| **Moidams** (Charaideo, Assam — Ahom mounds) | 2024 |
| **Maratha Military Landscapes of India** (12 forts, Maharashtra & Tamil Nadu) | 2025 |
| **Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath** (latest) | 2026 |

## Andhra Pradesh art & architecture

- **Amaravati school** — white-marble Buddhist reliefs (Krishna delta), under the **Satavahanas**; **Nagarjunakonda** Buddhist remains.
- **Lepakshi** — Veerabhadra temple (Vijayanagara): the **hanging pillar** and superb ceiling **murals**.
- **Srisailam (Mallikarjuna)** and **Tirupati** — major Dravidian temples of AP.
keyPoints: India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2026 (37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed — Khangchendzonga).
The first four Indian sites (1983) were Ajanta, Ellora, Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal.
Maratha Military Landscapes of India was inscribed in 2025; the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath (2026) is the latest.
Moidams (Charaideo, Assam) was inscribed in 2024 — the first cultural site from the North-East.
AP art: Amaravati marble Buddhist school (Satavahana), Lepakshi's hanging pillar & murals, Srisailam Dravidian temple.
items.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — India (whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/in), verified Sep 2026; APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture (AP examples)
